html:
The Marikana massacre took place on 16 August 2012 near a platinum mine of the company Lonmin at Marikana, northwest of Johannesburg, when police shot dead 34 striking miners.

Rock drill operators had walked out demanding higher wages, and violence in the days before had killed ten people, among them police officers and security guards. Police then fired on strikers gathered on a hill, and killed more of them as they fled among nearby rocks.

It was the deadliest use of force by the state since the end of apartheid, and recalled the Sharpeville massacre. A commission of inquiry criticised the police. The massacre damaged trust in the ANC government and its ties to the unions.
sum: The Marikana massacre took place on 16 August 2012 near a platinum mine of the company Lonmin at Marikana, northwest of Johannesburg, when police shot dead 34 striking miners.
